state.misconception_label: Struggles to visualise nets of 3D shapes

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I have: This is the net of a... ![A circle touching a sector](). I got Triangle because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Can you explain why you chose triangle as the shape for this net? What characteristics of the net led you to that conclusion?

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Um, I think I just looked at the pointy bit and thought it was like a triangle shape? But now that you're asking me, I'm not really sure how a net actually works - like, does it fold up into the shape that's already drawn, or is the shape supposed to come from all the pieces together?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Can you think of any real-life objects that have similar shapes to the net you drew? How do those objects fold or unfold to create the shape you see?

score.justification_pass1: The teacher asks open questions that require reasoning but never directly addresses the student's fundamental confusion about how nets work (revealed in Turn 2), and the student shows no improvement in understanding by the end of the dialogue.
score.justification_pass2: The teacher consistently uses probing questions to guide the student's thinking without ever directly stating the answer, which is a textbook example of the Socratic method.
